concepts.def: After the First World War the USA refused to join the League of Nations and turned inwards, raising tariffs and restricting immigration with quota laws.
Under Harding and Coolidge, low taxes, laissez-faire policies and protective tariffs supported the 1920s consumer boom in cars, radios and household goods.
Panic selling in October 1929 collapsed share prices, ruined speculators who had bought on the margin, and shattered confidence in banks and business.
President Hoover stressed 'rugged individualism' and voluntary action, and though he later set up the Reconstruction Finance Corporation in 1932, he opposed direct federal relief.
From 1933 FDR's alphabet agencies such as the CCC, AAA and TVA provided relief, jobs and reform, transforming the federal government's role.
Critics attacked from both sides: the Supreme Court struck down the NRA and AAA, while figures like Huey Long said reform did not go far enough.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The USA 1918-41 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The USA 1918-41 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The USA 1918-41.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What did Hoover mean by 'rugged individualism'?
options: People should overcome hardship through self-reliance rather than depend on government handouts
The government should employ everyone directly
Banks should be nationalised
America should join the League of Nations

mcqs.q: Which body declared parts of the New Deal, including the NRA and AAA, unconstitutional?
options: The Supreme Court
The Senate
The FBI
The League of Nations

mcqs.q: Which industry, symbolised by the Model T, powered much of the 1920s boom?
options: The motor industry
The railway industry
The airline industry
The computer industry

mcqs.q: Why did the USA restrict immigration with quota laws in the 1920s?
options: Fear of communism and prejudice against southern and eastern European immigrants fuelled demands for restriction
There was no more land available for settlement
The League of Nations ordered the restrictions
Immigrants were needed in Europe for rebuilding

mcqs.q: Did Hoover do nothing about the Depression?
options: Hoover launched the first New Deal in 1930.
Hoover acted more than his reputation suggests — the Reconstruction Finance Corporation lent to banks and businesses in 1932 — but he opposed direct federal relief, so he seemed uncaring.
Hoover did absolutely nothing while Americans starved.
Banks failed because the US dollar was abolished in 1930.

mcqs.q: Did everyone share in the 1920s boom?
options: Only farmers benefited from the 1920s boom.
All Americans grew richer during the Roaring Twenties.
No — farmers, Black Americans and workers in older industries like coal and textiles saw little benefit, and wealth remained very unevenly spread.
Hoover launched the first New Deal in 1930.

mcqs.q: Why did so many American banks fail between 1929 and 1933?
options: Hoover launched the first New Deal in 1930.
Banks had lent and speculated heavily, and panicking customers staged bank runs to withdraw deposits; with no federal deposit insurance until 1933, failures cascaded.
Banks failed because the US dollar was abolished in 1930.
The government deliberately closed the banks to punish speculators.
